{{Quote|Make it ''fifteen wupiupi'', and you have a ''bet!''|translated=1|Graxol Kelvyyn|<ref name="Podracing Tales" />}}
'''Graxol Kelvyyn''' was an [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Slaver/Legends|slave trader]] and an obsessive [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] active throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. His business was based on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], but pleasure frequently brought him to the world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]; there, Kelvyyn bet on [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]] events. Often on his [[Limb/Legends|arm]] was the [[Lethan/Legends|Lethan]] [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Shakka/Legends|Shakka]], his [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] love interest. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], they attended Tatooine's [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] Podrace and viewed the competition from the private box of Kelvyyn's friend, the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]].

Kelvyyn initially wagered that the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|racer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] would win the event. However, impressed with Watto's [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] slave [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], the Anx placed several bets on the boy after the competition began. When Skywalker won the race, Kelvyyn smugly demanded [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]] from Watto, who had shown little faith in his own slave. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] later, the [[sentientologist]] [[Tem Eliss]] mentioned Kelvyyn in his [[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life|academic writings]]; Eliss considered the slave trader a gentle and loving being who was nevertheless a dishonorable example of the Anx [[Species/Legends|species]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|The boy has ''spunk''. I wager he'll finish. What do you say to ''ten wupiupi'', Watto?''&raquo;<br />&laquo;Heh heh heh!'' Don't ''insult'' me, ''Graxol''. Make it ''twenty wupiupi!''''&raquo;<br />&laquo;Agreed.|translated=1|Graxol Kelvyyn and Watto, during the Boonta Eve Classic|<ref name="Podracing Tales" />}}
The [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Graxol Kelvyyn<ref name="ccg" /> lived during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> Operating from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], he was active as a [[Slaver/Legends|slave trader]] throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], where he sold [[Slavery/Legends|living cargo]] to [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] who in turn shipped the enslaved across much of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. An obsessive [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]], Kelvyyn frequently visited the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to attend and bet on [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]] events alongside his friend [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], a [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]].<ref name="gamer" /> At the Podraces, the two of them became acquainted with [[Diva Shaliqua/Legends|Diva Shaliqua]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]]/[[Theelin/Legends|Theelin]] [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrid]] enslaved by the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]].<ref name="diva">{{DB|character|divashaliqua|Shaliqua, Diva}}</ref>

[[File:Wattos_box.jpg|thumb|left|325px|Kelvyyn watches the Boonta Eve Classic from Watto's box.]]
Shortly before<ref name="gamer" /> [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Kelvyyn fell in love with his enslaved<ref name="gamer" /> dancer<ref name="RoguesGallery">{{InsiderCite|131|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: An Audience of Aliens}}</ref> [[Shakka/Legends|Shakka]], a [[Lethan/Legends|Lethan]] [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] female.<ref name="gamer" /> She<ref name="ActionFigure">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Action Figure Collection]]''</ref> became a fixture on his arm at social gatherings,<ref name="gamer" /> and in 32 [[Galactic Standard Time/Legends|BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> both of them attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] Podrace at Tatooine's [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]], wherein they joined Watto and several of the Toydarian's other associates in his private viewing box high above the racing track.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> Confident in the abilities of the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|racer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]], Kelvyyn wagered 50,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] that he would win the day's event.<ref name="hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|packtype=Cinema Scenes|pack=Watto's Box|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeicswattosbox.asp}}</ref>

[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], a [[Youngling/Legends|young]] Human enslaved by Watto, was also entered in the race, and when his [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] failed to start, Kelvyyn and his comrades laughed at the boy's misfortune. Skywalker persevered and got his [[Podracer/Legends|vehicle]] going,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> but Watto was sceptical that the ragtag machine would be able to finish the race. Kelvyyn and Watto's friend [[Weazel/Legends|Weazel]] both wagered twenty [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]] that Skywalker would in fact complete all three laps, and Watto eagerly took the bet. After Sebulba completed the first lap in record time, Watto offered ten wupiupi that he would set a record for the entire race; Kelvyyn upped the ante to fifteen and accepted.<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> The Anx made one further wager with Watto: that Skywalker would win the entire event.<ref name="ccg" /> As Kelvyyn watched anxiously,<ref name="hasbro" /> Skywalker overtook Sebulba and emerged the victor. Although a furious Watto argued with his guests,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> Kelvyyn and Weazel demanded payment.<ref name="Podracing Tales" />

Years later,<ref name="Galaxy Guide">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> Kelvyyn was discussed by the [[Iyra]] [[sentientologist]] [[Tem Eliss]] in ''[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life]]'',<ref name="gamer" /> a [[Book/Legends|book]] that showcased some of the galaxy's myriad [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> Kelvyyn was presented as an example of a dishonorable Anx whose gambling and slave trading were cited as vices.<ref name="gamer" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You owe ''me'' thirty-five wupiupi. Maybe ''next time'' you'll bet on ''your slave!''|translated=1|Kelvyyn taunts Watto following the Boonta Eve Classic|<ref name="Podracing Tales" />}}
[[File:Gamblingmen.png|thumb|right|250px|Kelvyyn continued to place bets after the Boonta Eve Classic began.]]
Graxol Kelvyyn was a skilled trader who dealt in slaves and maintained a network of seedy smugglers throughout the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. He was knowledgeable of the workings of criminal organizations and was adept at intimidating others.<ref name="gamer" /> However, Kelvyyn was also a gentle man<ref name="ccg" /> and was, with Shakka, a favorited local of the Tatooine [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]].<ref name="hasbro" /> Watto considered him a friend and enjoyed his company when watching podraces.<ref name="Kids15 (1999)">{{Kids1999Cite|15|Meet Watto!}}</ref> He fell in love with his slave Shakka, but [[Professor/Legends|Professor]] Tem Eliss nevertheless considered him a dishonorable individual and believed that falling for one's own property was a mistake that no slaver could afford to make.<ref name="gamer" />

A known aficionado of Podracing,<ref name="cswe">{{CSWECite|II|207|Kelvyyn, Graxol}}</ref> Kelvyyn enjoyed the risks and rewards of the races<ref name="ccg" /> and gambled on them obsessively.<ref name="gamer" /> He was not averse to raising a bet's stakes.<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> Kelvyyn made separate wagers on two different racers to win the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]]<ref name="ccg" /><ref name="hasbro" /> in 32 BBY<ref name="NEC" /> and continued to gamble with Watto after the race began.<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> Although he laughed and clapped when Anakin Skywalker's Podracer failed to start,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> he was afterward impressed with the boy's performance<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> and placed multiple bets on him.<ref name="ccg" /> Kelvyyn taunted Watto when failing to bet on his own slave lost the Toydarian money.<ref name="Podracing Tales" />

Kelvyyn was a [[Hair/Legends|hairless]] male Anx<ref name="ccg" /> with [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> and creamy white skin.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> He stood considerably taller than Watto's height of 1.37 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="Height" /> Able to fluently speak, read, and write both the [[Anx (language)/Legends|Anx language]] and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], Kelvyyn could additionally speak [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], [[Rodese/Legends|Rodese]], [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]], [[Shusugaunt (language)/Legends|Shusugaunt]], and [[Twi'leki/Legends|Twi'leki]].<ref name="gamer" />

==Skills and abilities==
Kelvyyn was trained in the use of [[Unarmed combat/Legends|martial arts]].<ref name="gamer" />

==Equipment==
Kelvyyn carried a [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|hold-out blaster]] on his person.<ref name="gamer" /> At the Boonta Eve Classic Podrace, Kelvyyn wore orange and blue [[Robe/Legends|robes]] with a high collar and a [[Necklace/Legends|necklace]].<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Creation===
{{Quote|And Jerome was in another character when the Pod Race audience set was filmed, so I got the chance to play Graxol Kelvyyn for that scene. That was nearly five hours in an oven, so it's great fun for a day but I'm not sure how the performers/actors put up with it for weeks at a time!|John Coppinger|<ref name="interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.scifinow.co.uk/interviews/star-wars-interview-john-coppinger/2|text=Star Wars interview: John Coppinger|work=SciFiNow|nobackup=1}}</ref>}}
[[File:Anxconcept.jpg|thumb|150px|Anx concept art by Doug Chiang served as the inspiration for Graxol Kelvyyn.]]
Graxol Kelvyyn was, along with [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Horox Ryyder/Legends|Horox Ryyder]], one of two Anx characters created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="interview" /> which premiered on [[May 19]], [[1999]].<ref name="YearByYear">''[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle]]''</ref> Both characters' origins lie in a piece of concept art drawn by artist [[Doug Chiang]] that was later turned into a 3D character maquette by sculptor [[John Coppinger]]; Coppinger added slight details and altered some of the characters' proportions in order for the transition from drawing to sculpture to work. A nearly eleven-foot-tall Anx costume was then created that required actor [[Jerome Blake]] to stand on twenty-four-inch stilts with the costume's head resting thirty-six inches above his own.<ref name="interview" />

Coppinger stood in for Blake during some of the early Anx costume fittings and demonstrated the costume's rig to director [[George Lucas]], who, worried that the character was too tall, saw to it that both Kelvyyn and Ryyder sat down during their scenes in the movie. The character's scenes were shot at [[Leavesden Studios]]<ref name="Filming">{{InsiderCite|39|When Artoo Met Wicket}}</ref> in [[Wikipedia:Watford|Watford]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]].<ref name="Location">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/bts/production/news19970929.html|text=First Phase Of Episode I Production Wraps At Leavesden Studios}}</ref> During filiming, Blake was busy playing another role, and Coppinger donned the Anx costume in his stead. Coppinger has described the experience as "nearly five hours in an oven," but still "great fun for a day."<ref name="interview" /> Coppinger's performance went uncredited in the film and<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> was incorrectly attributed to Blake in the article "[[In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Jerome Blake]]," published in [[Star Wars Insider 48|forty-eighth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine<ref name="Insider 48">{{InsiderCite|48|In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Jerome Blake}}</ref> on [[April 4]], [[2000]].<ref name="Fan">{{SWArchive|url=community/news/2000/03/news20000313.html|text=Star Wars Insider #48}}</ref>

The character was revealed on [[May 3]], 1999,<ref name="Collector">{{CollectorCite|6|Around the Galaxy}}</ref> on a card released by collectable company [[Topps]] in their first series of [[1999 Topps Star Wars: Episode I Widevision Series 1|Star Wars: Episode I Widevision]] cards.<ref name="Intergalactic">{{Topps|set=1999 Topps Star Wars: Episode I Widevision Series 1|cardname=47 - Intergalactic Spectators|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/73014/cid/5263457/1999-Topps-Widevision-Star-Wars:-Episode-I-47-Intergalactic-Spectators}}</ref> Kelvyyn then first appeared in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|adaptation]] for Episode I,<ref name="video game" /> which released the day before the film<ref name="YearByYear" /> on [[May 18]], 1999.<ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/1999/05/18/star-wars-hits-the-shelves|text=Star Wars Hits The Shelves|author=IGN Staff|date=1999-05-18|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|archivedate=20121121210047}}</ref> An action figure of Kelvyyn was released by [[Hasbro]] later in 1999 and was packaged with figures of Watto and Shakka in a three-pack called "Watto's Box;" the set was the first licensed ''[[Star Wars]]'' product to provide the character with the name "Graxol Kelvyyn."<ref name="hasbro" /> At the time, Kelvyyn was the largest ''Star Wars'' figure that Hasbro had ever produced.<ref name="Insider 48" /> 

===Discrepancies===
[[File:HoroxRyyder2-SWCTP.png|thumb|left|200px|Sources have confused Graxol Kelvyyn for Senator Horox Ryyder (pictured).]]
More information on the character was later revealed in the [[2001]] ''[[Coruscant Limited]]'' expansion set of [[Decipher]]'s [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]].<ref name="ccg" /> Although the Hasbro toy set asserts that Kelvyyn bet on Sebulba to win the Boonta Eve Classic,<ref name="hasbro" /> ''Coruscant Limited'' states that he wagered Skywalker would achieve victory.<ref name="ccg" /> As Kelvyyn has been established as an obsessive gambler,<ref name="gamer" /> this article treats both statements as [[canon]]ical.

Kelvyyn is involved in several discrepancies between ''The Phantom Menace'' and the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]. In the video game adaptation, Kelvyyn and Watto are in the Toydarian's box prior to the Boonta Eve Classic when the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] enters and gambles with Watto on the outcome of the race. This encounter contradicts the events of the film,<ref name="video game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> which sees the bet occur in the Podracers' [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] and without Kelvyyn present.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> The game also presents a different roster of characters seen in the box during the race; although Kelvyyn is among them, he is unaccompanied by Shakka.<ref name="video game" /> Furthermore, the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] ''[[Podracing Tales]]'', illustrated by [[Ken Steacy]]<ref name="Podracing Tales" /> and published on [[December 19]], 2000,<ref name="Date2">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/comics/darkhorse/dhSer_podracing.asp|text=Podracing Tales|archivedate=20190730111721}}</ref> depicts Kelvyyn with considerably greener skin than in ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="Podracing Tales" />

"[[The Creature King]]," an article written by [[Kristin Lund]] and published in the [[May]] 2000 [[Star Wars Kids (1999) 9|ninth]] issue of the [[Star Wars Kids (1999)|1999 newsstand run]] of ''[[Star Wars Kids (disambiguation)|Star Wars Kids]]'' magazine, incorrectly states Kelvynn is Horox Ryyder.<ref name="TheKing">{{Kids1999Cite|9|The Creature King}}</ref> The [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 86|eighty-sixth issue]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'',<ref name="Fact File" /> published around [[August 20]], [[2003]],<ref name="Date">{{FFdates|86}}</ref> made the same mistake and posited that the Senator's presence in Watto's box is surprising.<ref name="Fact File">{{FactFile|86|RYY 1-2|Horox Ryyder}}</ref>
